## Overview:
The PR simplifies message subscription by using an inline callback in `mount()`. It changes `unmount()` to only clear the stored socket reference, removing the previous explicit listener deregistration.

## Strengths:
- Small, focused diff.
- Preserves the existing message-to-`render` behavior in `mount()`.

## Risk areas:
- The anonymous listener is no longer available to `off()`, so unmounting may leave the socket subscribed and continue rendering after unmount.
- Repeated mount/unmount cycles may accumulate listeners and cause duplicate renders or resource leaks.
- No tests are shown for listener cleanup or lifecycle behavior.

## P3/nit candidates:
- None.

resolvedReview.overview:
This PR reworks the `SocketView` subscription lifecycle in `src/socket-view.ts`. `mount()` previously stored the message handler on the instance (`this.onMessage`) and registered it with `socket.on`; `unmount()` detached it via `this.socket?.off("message", this.onMessage)`. The new code registers an inline anonymous closure in `mount()` and reduces `unmount()` to clearing the stored socket reference.

Despite the PR description ("preserving existing contracts"), the change breaks the existing lifecycle contract: because the anonymous listener is never stored anywhere, `unmount()` can no longer deregister it, so the socket keeps a live reference to the view after unmounting. This is a blocking regression; the rest of the diff is fine.

findings.title: [P1] Restore message-listener removal in `unmount`
findings.body: Triggered by any `mount(socket)` → `unmount()` cycle followed by further socket activity. The new `mount()` registers an anonymous closure (`socket.on("message", message => this.render(message))`) whose reference is never kept, and the new `unmount()` only does `this.socket = undefined` — the previous `this.socket?.off("message", this.onMessage)` deregistration is gone. Since `off()` requires the exact handler reference, the listener can no longer be detached at all. Consequences: an unmounted view keeps rendering on every subsequent `"message"` event; repeated mount/unmount cycles accumulate one closure per mount and amplify each message into multiple `render` calls; and any socket that outlives the view retains the view and its closure, preventing garbage collection. Restore the stored-handler pattern (or equivalent) so `unmount()` can actually detach the listener.

# PR Review

**Verdict:** request_changes

## Overview

This PR reworks the `SocketView` subscription lifecycle in `src/socket-view.ts`. `mount()` previously stored the message handler on the instance (`this.onMessage`) and registered it with `socket.on`; `unmount()` detached it via `this.socket?.off("message", this.onMessage)`. The new code registers an inline anonymous closure in `mount()` and reduces `unmount()` to clearing the stored socket reference.

Despite the PR description ("preserving existing contracts"), the change breaks the existing lifecycle contract: because the anonymous listener is never stored anywhere, `unmount()` can no longer deregister it, so the socket keeps a live reference to the view after unmounting. This is a blocking regression; the rest of the diff is fine.

## Verification

Verification was not run: `pr_review_verify` list returned `enabled: false` — no user-level `verificationBaselines` are configured, so there is no trusted baseline to execute. (Note: baseline execution runs unsandboxed PR code and requires an explicit opt-in profile; an external sandbox/container is recommended for untrusted PRs when enabled.) All findings below are instead confirmed by direct source inspection of the diff and surrounding repository.

## Findings

### [P1] Restore message-listener removal in `unmount`
**Severity:** P1
**Rationale:** Triggered by any `mount(socket)` → `unmount()` cycle followed by further socket activity. The new `mount()` registers an anonymous closure (`socket.on("message", message => this.render(message))`) whose reference is never kept, and the new `unmount()` only does `this.socket = undefined` — the previous `this.socket?.off("message", this.onMessage)` deregistration is gone. Since `off()` requires the exact handler reference, the listener can no longer be detached at all. Consequences: an unmounted view keeps rendering on every subsequent `"message"` event; repeated mount/unmount cycles accumulate one closure per mount and amplify each message into multiple `render` calls; and any socket that outlives the view retains the view and its closure, preventing garbage collection. Restore the stored-handler pattern (or equivalent) so `unmount()` can actually detach the listener.
**Location:** `src/socket-view.ts:14-18 RIGHT`

### [P3] Add listener-lifecycle regression coverage with the fix
**Severity:** P3
**Rationale:** The repository contains no tests (and no test infrastructure) for `SocketView`, and this PR changes exactly the behavior most in need of protection — listener registration/detachment. When fixing the P1 above, add a regression test that emits a `"message"` event after `unmount()` and asserts rendering no longer occurs. Rated P3 rather than higher because the absence of any test setup is a pre-existing repo-wide condition, not something this PR introduced.

### [nit] Confirm the intended contract for an unreferenced `SocketView`
**Severity:** nit
**Rationale:** A source-wide search finds no callers of `SocketView` outside `src/socket-view.ts` itself, so no in-repo usage validates whether weakening `unmount()` was intentional. Worth confirming the intended lifecycle contract before merge, since the PR description claims existing contracts are preserved.

## Lane completeness

All requested lanes completed. All six `--full` passes (overview, conventions-maintainability, correctness, correctness-contracts, security-performance, performance-resources) returned `status: complete` with no partial, timed-out, or failed lanes.

## Strengths and notes

- Small, focused diff; the `mount()` message-to-`render` wiring itself is preserved correctly.
- Four independent lanes (correctness, conventions, security, performance) converged on the same single root cause — the anonymous listener that `unmount()` can no longer remove — and no other defects were found; the contracts lane found no type/compile/boundary issues introduced.

**Notes:**
- Correctness: unmount no longer detaches the socket listener; stale views keep rendering and listeners accumulate across remounts (P1 above).
- Security: the retained closure means untrusted socket messages continue reaching `render` after unmount — folded into the P1 rather than a separate finding.
- Performance: memory retention (view + closure held by a live socket) and duplicated renders per message across mount cycles — same root defect, no additional resource issue found.
